title: Lesson 1: See, Think, Wonder: What Are We Thankful For?
objective: Students will identify and describe items of gratitude and explain what families celebrate during harvest festivals.

activities.title: See-Think-Wonder: Hands of Gratitude
activities.prompt: Display the opening illustration on page 24. Guide students to examine the objects held in the hands using the 3-step thinking routine.
activities.text: Look at the picture on page 24. What do you see? What do you think about the objects? What do you wonder about thankfulness?
activities.answer: Students identify the video game controller, soccer ball, house, sunshine, and sweets, connecting them to gratitude.

activities.title: Think, Pair, Share: When Do You Say Thank You?
activities.prompt: Have students discuss in pairs when they express thanks and what they are grateful for in their own homes.
activities.text: Talk with your partner: 'When do you say thank you?' Use the model: 'I think he is thankful for his home. I am thankful for my family.'
activities.answer: Oral pair-share and class report.

activities.title: Photo Preview: The Chuseok Family
activities.prompt: Direct students to photograph E on page 25 showing a Korean family in hanbok with autumn crops.
activities.text: Where is this family? What special clothes are they wearing? What foods are on the table?
activities.answer: In Korea; wearing hanbok; autumn fruits and grains for harvest.

title: Lesson 2: Reading 1: Chuseok, Korea's Harvest Festival
objective: Students will read aloud and track the origin of Chuseok and its ancient weaving contest.

activities.title: Choral Reading: The Ancient Weaving Contest
activities.prompt: Model reading page 26 with expressive intonation. Have students track with fingers and read aloud together.
activities.text: Two teams have a contest to find out who can weave the most cloth. They weave for a whole month! On the full moon night, the king comes and gives a big feast.
activities.answer: Students read fluently and answer: Who won the contest? (The king announced the winner and treated both teams to a feast).

activities.title: Text Tracking: Modern Chuseok Today
activities.prompt: Read page 27 together. Ask students to highlight details about how long Chuseok lasts and where people go.
activities.text: How long does Chuseok last? Where do people go? Why do they go home?
activities.answer: It lasts three days at the end of summer; people travel home to celebrate with family and give thanks.

title: Lesson 3: Words in Context: Celebrating the Harvest
objective: Students will define and apply target vocabulary words in meaningful spoken and written sentences.

activities.title: Target Word Discovery
activities.prompt: Guide students to locate each highlighted word on page 27 and match it with visual gestures and simple definitions.

words.def: To make cloth by crossing threads over and under.
Material used to make clothes and blankets.
A game or competition to see who wins.
A special celebration with food and fun.
Gathering ripe vegetables and fruits from fields.
Family members who lived long ago.

activities.answer: Students complete physical action gestures (weaving fingers, clapping for contest, bowing for ancestors).

activities.title: Sentence Frame Fill
activities.prompt: Provide sentence frames for students to fill with target words.
activities.text: 1. Two teams had a ___ to weave the most ___. 2. People celebrate the autumn ___ at the Chuseok ___.
activities.answer: 1. contest, cloth; 2. harvest, festival.

title: Lesson 4: Comprehension & Traditions: Food, Dance, and Ceremony
objective: Students will describe key Chuseok customs and complete the graphic organizer on page 30.

activities.title: Close Reading: Songpyeon, Dances, and Ancestors
activities.prompt: Read pages 28-29 closely with students, examining photos of songpyeon, the circle dance (Ganggangsullae), and the charye table.
activities.text: What are songpyeon? What do people do in the circle dance? Why do families bow in the ceremony?
activities.answer: Songpyeon are special sweet rice cakes; women hold hands and dance in a circle; families bow to show love and respect for ancestors.

activities.title: Explore the Reading: Songpyeon Organizer
activities.prompt: Guide students to complete Activity A on page 30 by writing 4 ways people celebrate Chuseok.
activities.text: Fill in the four songpyeon shapes: How do people celebrate Chuseok?
activities.answer: 1. Buy new clothes. 2. Make and eat songpyeon. 3. Dance and play games. 4. Remember ancestors with a ceremony.

activities.title: Sentence Completion: Being Thankful
activities.prompt: Students write complete answers for Activity B on page 30.
activities.text: 1. Korean people are thankful for ___. 2. They are also thankful for ___.
activities.answer: 1. the food from the harvest; 2. their family / ancestors.

title: Lesson 5: Reading Skill: Understanding the Setting
objective: Students will identify setting as time and place and explain how setting influences a character's emotions.

activities.title: Concept Focus: What is Setting?
activities.prompt: Read the definition box on page 31: 'The setting is the time and place in the story. One story can have many different settings.'
activities.text: Look at Clara in the three pictures: 1. Climbing high outside. 2. On the sofa with a book. 3. Looking out the window at rain. How does each place make her feel?
activities.answer: 1. Scared / nervous; 2. Laughing / happy; 3. Sad / crying.

activities.title: Compare Settings: Venn Diagram
activities.prompt: Complete the Venn diagram on page 31 comparing 'In the Kitchen' and 'On the Farm'.
activities.text: Sort the words: fruit, vegetables, family, outside, plants, inside, bowls into the diagram.
activities.answer: Kitchen: family, inside, bowls; Farm: outside, plants; Both: fruit, vegetables.

title: Lesson 6: Reading 2: First Harvest on Mars
objective: Students will read and track the science fiction story 'First Harvest' and describe the unusual crops.

activities.title: Story Tracking: Part 1 - The Colorful Harvest
activities.prompt: Read pages 32-33 aloud. Have students look closely at the crops in the illustration and text.
activities.text: Harvest time is here! What strange colors are the crops? What did Dad worry about?
activities.answer: Pink potatoes, purple corn, striped tomatoes, orange peas, purple carrots; Dad was worried because water was scarce.

activities.title: Words in Context: Farm Actions & Features
activities.prompt: Direct students to the vocabulary box on page 33.

words.def: To pull fruit from a plant.
Feeling afraid or anxious about a problem.
To feel sure that something is real.

activities.answer: Students read and use each word in a spoken sentence.

activities.title: Story Tracking: Part 2 - Planning the Feast
activities.prompt: Read pages 34-35. Highlight Ruth's idea and Mom's baking plan.
activities.text: What does Ruth suggest? What does Mom want to bake?
activities.answer: Ruth suggests getting everyone together for a feast; Mom wants to make an apple pie.

title: Lesson 7: Skill Practice & Speaking: Space Suits and Secret Settings
objective: Students will uncover the story's Martian setting, master phonics with -st, and describe space survival.

activities.title: The Big Reveal: Astronauts on Mars!
activities.prompt: Read pages 36-37. Direct students to the helmets labeled 'MARS 3000' and the oxygen warning.
activities.text: Where is the family really living? What must Ruth and August check before playing outside?
activities.answer: They live on Mars! They must check their space suits and make sure they have a lot of air.

activities.title: Phonics Lab: Ending Blend -st
activities.prompt: Read and drill the -st ending words on page 38: fast, last, lost, best, test. Hunt for -st words in the reading.
activities.text: Listen and say: fast, last, lost, best, test. Find two words ending with -st in 'First Harvest'!
activities.answer: Target reading words: harvest, first.

activities.title: Discussion: Farming on Mars
activities.prompt: Lead a group discussion on Activity B on page 38: 'Why is it hard to grow food on Mars?'
activities.text: What does a plant need that Mars does not have naturally?
activities.answer: Mars has no liquid water, no breathable air/oxygen, freezing temperatures, and barren rocks.

title: Lesson 8: Think Together: Harvest Connections & Reading Journal
objective: Students will compare Earth and Mars harvest celebrations, write a creative sequel in their journal, and complete an exit check.

activities.title: Compare and Contrast: Earth vs Mars Harvests
activities.prompt: Guide students to complete the chart on page 39 comparing Chuseok and First Harvest.
activities.text: What's the same in both stories? What's different?
activities.answer: Same: Families celebrate together, share big feasts, give thanks for hard work. Different: Chuseok is a traditional Korean festival on Earth; First Harvest is a futuristic sci-fi harvest on Mars.

activities.title: My Reading Journal: What Happens Next?
activities.prompt: Students choose either story and write 2-3 sentences and draw what happens after the ending.
activities.text: Choose Chuseok or First Harvest. Read the ending again. Write and draw what happens next!
activities.answer: Creative student writing and drawing.

activities.title: 10-Minute Exit Check
activities.prompt: Quick oral and written wrap-up check for all students.
activities.text: 1. Name 2 things people eat at Chuseok. 2. What is the setting of First Harvest? 3. Say a word ending in -st.
activities.answer: 1. Songpyeon, harvest fruit; 2. Mars / indoor farm; 3. fast / best / first / harvest.
